g.text: Classification rules (three independent signals)
Every project gets a category only when independent sources agree. Any disagreement gets no OAR, so a dispute can
only lower a company's estimated real tonnes, never raise it.
Berkeley VROD curated project Type (PROJECTS sheet, 11,856 projects), joined by project ID (Verra VCS, Gold
Standard GS). Join rate: 100% of rows and tonnes.
CarbonPlan OffsetsDB project_type (independent classification, parquet release; covers 78.2% of retired tonnes
with a known type).
Registry methodology code (REDD+: VM0004/6/7/9/15/37/48; biomass cookstoves: VMR0006, AMS-II.G, VM0050,
TPDDTEC, improved-cookstove and metered GS methodologies; grid renewables: ACM0002, AMS-I.D, AMS-I.F,
Type to OAR category: REDD+ -> REDD+; Cookstoves -> cookstoves, except solar cookers, coal-ignition, LPG and
stove-plus-water projects (Probst's cookstove studies cover biomass cookstoves only); HFC23 Destruction ->
HFC-23; Improved Forest Management -> US IFM only in the US; Wind in China -> China wind; other wind, hydro,
solar, geothermal, RE bundled, biomass -> renewables (no OAR); everything else -> no OAR. VROD's SF6
Replacement is not SF6 destruction and gets no OAR.
Result on VROD v2026-08 (since 2020): 234 projects (6.15% of tonnes) have at least one disagreeing signal; all are set
to no OAR and listed in data/classification_review.csv. None of these disputes removed an OAR that
Berkeley's type would have given; they are projects Berkeley already places outside the OAR categories while
another signal points to one. The largest are Katingan (VCS1477) and Sumatra Merang (VCS1899): REDD+ according to
OffsetsDB and the VM0007 code, Wetland Restoration according to Berkeley. Neither is in Probst's REDD+ sample (Latin
America, Africa, Cambodia), so no OAR is applied. Automated checks live in the __main__ block of
pipeline/build.py.
